The walky-talky of the staff which is used to co-ordinate amongst themselves is extremely annoying and cuts the ways in your happy converstations. It can be easily replaced by attaching an earpiece. The table management of the staff was impressive though.
The overall experience was decent. It is a very good option for vegeterian food among many vegeterian restaurants in Kandivali.

featured_reviews.name: The foodie world
featured_reviews.review_text:
Achija in Kandivali East is one of those classic family restaurants that never disappoints. While it’s most famous for its pav bhaji, my visit turned out to be a complete feast with a mix of flavors. The pav bhaji with butter garlic chutney truly lived up to the hype—rich, buttery, and perfectly spiced, with that chutney taking it to another level. The paneer hotpan was sizzling and full of flavor, while the Mexican cheese roll was cheesy, crunchy, and indulgent. For South Indian cravings, the thatte idli was soft, fluffy, and really comforting.

On the drinks side, the pink guava and peach ice tea were refreshing and balanced, and the Kit Kat shake was a fun, chocolatey treat to end the meal. Achija is definitely a place where you can enjoy a wide variety of dishes under one roof, making it perfect for family outings. The vibe is casual, the food is consistently good, and the menu has something for everyone.

featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Pop Tates on a Friday evening mainly for the food. The place was completely crowded and very lively, with a cricket match playing, which added to the vibe. Since we weren’t there to drink, we just had water, and I ordered a ginger ale.
For starters, we wanted something spicy, so we asked for a chicken starter. The waiter suggested the Jamaican Jerk Chicken. It was not spicy at all and was slightly on the sweeter side, but it still tasted good on its own.
Next, we ordered Devil’s Paneer. The paneer was very soft and juicy, with a mild hint of spice. Not very spicy, but nicely done.
The Prawns Chilli was really good. The prawns felt fresh, were full of flavour, and again mildly spicy rather than hot.
We also ordered Cheesy Mushroom Bruschetta, which was rich, creamy, and very cheesy. The bruschetta was well toasted, and the combination worked really well.

Then we ordered for Tom Yum Soup. Now this was the worst soup we ever had. It tasted like a bad watery Tomato Rasam. I am sorry but yeah it was just bad.

For the main course, we ordered a Chicken Shashlik Sizzler and a Mexican Grilled Chicken Sizzler. The quantity was shockingly huge. The chicken was tender, well-seasoned, and full of flavour. The accompaniments that came with the sizzlers were also very good.
Overall, the food was excellent, the service was quick, and the staff were very attentive. Orders were taken and served promptly.
I would definitely visit Pop Tates again when I’m back in Mumbai but I have to deduct a star coz of the soup.

The prices are reasonable, making it accessible for all dosa lovers. Whether you're a dosa aficionado or trying it for the first time, this food stall in Thakur Village is a must-visit. I can't wait to return for more mouthwatering dosas!

Fantastic Family Dinner Experience at Mira’s Veg Restaurant!

We recently went to Mira’s Veg Restaurant for a family dinner, and it was a delightful experience. The food was simply awesome, and the ambience had a simple, minimal, and charming old-school vibe that we loved.

We ordered a variety of dishes, including multiple soups, paneer and veg starters, veg and paneer sabzis, butter rotis, and matka biryani. The Manchow and Tamatar soups were outstanding—flavorful and served in generous portions. The highlight of the meal was the Matka Biryani, which was absolutely mind-blowing and delicious.

All the food was served promptly, and everything tasted fantastic. This is a pure veg restaurant we highly recommend to anyone looking for delicious food and a welcoming atmosphere. Perfect for family outings!
